comparison: Both evaluate assay development and statistical validation (C22-C32). OpenEval finds all claims SUPPORTED with proper statistical justification. Peer review rates UNCERTAIN due to concerns about positive control inconsistencies (DAPT vs RO4929097 showing different effects) and initially 'sloppily described' statistical methodology, though improvements were acknowledged in revision.

Both evaluate primary screen results and hit categorization (C33-C41). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED with clear documentation. Peer review rates UNCERTAIN due to concerns that secondary islet effects may represent 'global increase in neurod:GFP expression...not confined to the pancreas' and potential 'artifact of the transgenic reporter system' rather than true secondary islets.

Both evaluate validation results using orthogonal transgenic lines (C42-C43). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED due to 55% validation rate and independent reporter confirmation. Peer review rates UNCERTAIN due to concerns about neurod:GFP increases 'not confined to the pancreas' and questions about counting consistency across experiments.

Both evaluate paroxetine validation and cell-type specificity (C44-C46). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with appropriate statistical tests. Peer review rates UNCERTAIN due to baseline instability concerns (DMSO controls varying from 29 to 33-35 β cells across experiments) and inappropriate use of 'serial t-tests' without multiple comparison correction when detecting 'relatively modest effects'.

Both evaluate NF-κB mechanism (C47-C54). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED through convergent evidence from multiple pathway inhibitors. Peer review rates UNCERTAIN, finding the story 'not terribly convincing' because thioctic acid and parthenolide are 'not exactly NF-κB go-to compounds' and other compounds 'barely described' without dose-response data. Concerns about compound specificity remain partially addressed despite revision.

OpenEval R7 evaluates NF-κB/Notch co-localization (C55-C56) and finds SUPPORTED, though notes functional relationship requires further investigation. Peer R6 addresses broader NF-κB mechanism including these claims, rating UNCERTAIN with concerns about reporter validation and whether inhibitors decrease EGFP in ductal progenitors as claimed.

Both evaluate serotonergic mechanism and proliferation (C57-C62). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with convergent pharmacological evidence and EdU data. Peer review rates UNCERTAIN, questioning whether β cell increases result from 'impaired insulin signaling' rather than direct effects, challenging proliferation interpretation ('data in Figure 6B does not support that β cell replication plays a major role'), and questioning serotonin antibody validation.

OpenEval R9 evaluates glucose control experiments (C66-C68) and finds SUPPORTED, strengthening direct proliferation mechanism. Peer R7 addresses this within broader serotonergic evaluation, expressing concern that 'glucose was measured...after 3 days' rather than within first day of treatment, leaving mechanism (direct vs. indirect glucose effects) uncertain.

OpenEval R10 evaluates cross-species validation (C69-C73) and finds SUPPORTED with appropriate statistical tests demonstrating evolutionary conservation. Peer R7 includes these claims in broader serotonergic evaluation rated UNCERTAIN, with concerns about mechanism and interpretation (proliferation vs. differentiation from replicated progenitors) affecting confidence in cross-species findings.

Both evaluate comparative findings with concurrent work (C79-C83). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED, noting validation through Tsuji et al. overlap and expanded discovery of additional mechanisms. Peer review also rates SUPPORTED, accepting these as contextual findings that validate the screening approach without substantive critique.

Both evaluate platform novelty and scale (C1-C2, C74). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED based on >500,000 larvae screen demonstrating HTS capabilities. Peer review also rates SUPPORTED, with all three reviewers explicitly acknowledging 'first true HTS screen performed in a vertebrate organism' and finding 'high-throughputness most impressive.' Peer R1 also includes validation rate claims (C75-C78) not in OpenEval R1.

OpenEval R11 evaluates screening success metrics (C3, C75-C76, C78) and finds SUPPORTED with high validation rate. Peer R1 includes some of these claims (C75-C76, C78) within broader platform evaluation, rating SUPPORTED without substantive critique of validation rates.

OpenEval R11 addresses screening success (C3, C75-C76, C78). Peer R8 evaluates major biological discoveries (C3-C5), rating UNCERTAIN. While reviewers acknowledge findings as 'interesting' and identifying 'new regulators of β-cell mass,' novelty is tempered by observation that 'serotonin pathway is already well described' and concerns about NF-κB story undermine confidence.

Both evaluate major biological discoveries (C4-C5). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED based on mechanistic validation and cross-species conservation. Peer review rates UNCERTAIN, acknowledging findings as 'interesting' but noting serotonin pathway 'already well described' and expressing reservations about mechanistic interpretation and statistical rigor that affect confidence in novelty claims.

Both evaluate compound library composition (C97-C100). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED as explicitly stated methodological details. Peer review also rates SUPPORTED, accepting these descriptive claims without challenge as supporting study design.

OpenEval R17 evaluates practical advantages including FDA-approved rate (C95-C96, C77). Peer R10 addresses translational potential (C95-C96) within broader library evaluation, rating SUPPORTED without challenging these claims about screening approach advantages.

OpenEval R17 includes sensitivity estimate (C77) among practical advantages, finding SUPPORTED. Peer R1 includes C77 within platform evaluation, rating SUPPORTED without substantive critique of sensitivity claims.

OpenEval R14 evaluates supporting literature for NF-κB findings (C84-C86), finding SUPPORTED as properly cited context strengthening biological plausibility. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific literature citation claims.

OpenEval R15 evaluates extensive supporting literature for serotonergic effects (C63-C65, C87-C91), finding SUPPORTED with proper citations providing biological context. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific literature citation claims.

OpenEval R16 evaluates acknowledgment of limitations and uncertainties in clinical translation (C92-C94), finding SUPPORTED as appropriate scientific caution. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these limitation acknowledgment claims.

OpenEval R19 evaluates background context and study rationale (C6-C11), finding SUPPORTED with proper citations establishing zebrafish model validity. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims.

OpenEval R20 evaluates established zebrafish pancreatic biology background (C12-C18), finding SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background biology claims.

OpenEval R21 evaluates methodological details including RO4929097/DAPT equivalence (C101-C102), finding SUPPORTED as standard practices. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though peer R2 raised concerns about inconsistent effects between DAPT and RO4929097 in different experiments.
